input: Read /doc/README.md and generate a table of contents from its headings (lines starting with # or ##). Insert the TOC after the first heading, formatted as a markdown list with '- [Heading Text](#anchor)' where anchor is the heading text lowercased with spaces replaced by hyphens. Write the result back to the file.

transcript.final_response:
I added a table of contents to `/doc/README.md`, right after the first heading (`# Project Alpha`), and saved the file:

```markdown
- [Project Alpha](#project-alpha)
- [Installation](#installation)
- [Usage](#usage)
- [API Reference](#api-reference)
- [Contributing](#contributing)
```

The list includes all five `#` and `##` headings, including the title itself. Each link anchor is the heading text in lowercase with spaces replaced by hyphens. I left a blank line before and after the list so the rest of the document is unchanged.
tool_calls:
cd /doc
toc=$(grep -E '^##? ' README.md | while IFS= read -r l; do t="${l#\#}"; t="${t#\#}"; t="${t# }"; a=$(echo "$t" | tr 'A-Z' 'a-z' | tr ' ' '-'); echo "- [$t](#$a)"; done)
{ head -n1 README.md; echo; echo "$toc"; tail -n +2 README.md; } > /tmp/r.md && mv /tmp/r.md README.md
cat README.md
